sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: 3H-mepyramine radioligand binding and histamine-stimulated 3H-inositol phosphate accumulation in CHO-K1 cells: Myc-H1 and Myc-GFP H1 pharmacology identical to wild-type H1R.
sites.rationale: HRH1 has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–27 as extracellular and residues 472–487 as intracellular, making the N-terminus the only extracellular terminus. The paper names no residue number, so position_evidence is topology_derived and insert_after_residue is 0 (prepend before Met1). Python confirmed seq[0]='M' (residue 1) and that TM1 begins at residue 28, leaving a 27-residue extracellular buffer well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. The published Myc-tagged construct retained full pharmacology, providing the highest validation tier. Full-length human H1R with an N-terminal myc tag (Myc-H1) and a dual N-terminal myc / C-terminal GFP version (Myc-GFP H1) were stably expressed in CHO-K1 cells. No specific residue number is named; 'N-terminal' is the only description of placement. The N-terminus (residues 1–27) is the sole extracellular terminus of H1R (C-terminus is intracellular, residues 472–487), so the junction is unambiguously the prepend position before Met1. Corroborated by L2/L4, which describe an independently constructed N-terminal HA-tagged H1R that was functional in HEK293T NFAT-luciferase assays.

sources.claim: The aim of the present study was to investigate the cellular pathway involved in histamine-stimulated internalization of the human H1-receptor in CHO-K1 cells expressing N-terminal myc-tagged H1-receptor (Myc-H1) or N-terminal myc-C-terminal green fluorescent protein (Myc-GFP H1) versions of the receptor. Studies of 3H-mepyramine binding and histamine-stimulated 3H-inositol phosphate accumulation in these cells showed that the Myc-H1 and Myc-GFP H1-receptors had identical pharmacology to the wild-type H1-receptor.

literature_notes: L2 and L4 describe the same N-terminal HA-H1R construct at the same junction (prepend before Met1) and corroborate L1 but do not add a second site. L3 describes an engineered structural construct in which ICL3 (residues 217–408, intracellular) was replaced by mBRIL and the C-terminal residues 484–487 (intracellular) were replaced by a K3-ALFA tag; both insertions are cytoplasmic and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 87–100, ECL2 166–187, ECL3 438–450), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: ICL3 residues 217–408 were deleted and replaced by mBRIL in a structural engineering construct; this loop falls within the intracellular span 212–416 and is not a surface-tag site.
C-terminal residues 484–487 were replaced by a K3-ALFA tag in the same structural construct; this region falls within the intracellular C-terminal span 472–487 and is not a surface-tag site.
